To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the odds of a case (19-30 year age group) initiating the habit of tobacco use is nearly 4 times more when the father is a tobacco user, and nearly 2 times more when the mother has no formal education.
the odds of a case (19-30 year old Tobacco user) initiating the habit of smoking is nearly four times more than controls when the parent is a Tobacco user (OR 3.99, 95% CI, (2.38 – 6.67)).
parental use of Tobacco and low parental warmth (especially father) are the two most important predictors for initiation of Tobacco use among children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the factors that influence the initiation of Tobacco usage in young adults, and in the process, we have identified the importance of parenting in the process.
the influence of parental Tobacco habits and parenting style on Tobacco use among the offspring.
the intergenerational transmission of Tobacco habits from parent to offspring, and how the parenting style may modify this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parental influence is a strong modifiable determinant of Tobacco use among young adults.
a child is more likely to initiate Tobacco use if the father is a Tobacco user, has a low warmth/care towards the child, the mother is uneducated and the child has a low self esteem.
parental use of Tobacco is an important risk factor for the initiation of Tobacco use amongst young adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intergenerational transmission of Tobacco habits is more likely to occur in families with low paternal warmth and low maternal education.
parental influence on the child is an important risk factor in the uptake of Tobacco use.
the intergenerational transmission of Tobacco habits from parent to child is mediated by the father’s parenting style and mother’s educational status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low bonding with the father is a significant risk factor for Tobacco uptake among young adults.
the father’s parenting style and mother’s level of education are important factors to be considered when designing interventions for Tobacco use prevention.
parents need to be educated about the ill effects of their own Tobacco use on their children, and the importance of a positive parenting style.
